claims.text: The actual distance is governed by the trace, and the trace records 27.18 km against a booked optimal of 21.0 km — an excess of 6.18 km, or 29.4%. That clears both POL-RD-01 establishment tests at once: more than 20% of optimal (4.2 km) and more than 0.8 km in absolute terms. The route deviation is established on this trip's own telemetry, and the driver's 27.2 km convenience copy on the trip record is not the figure the threshold test runs on.

With the deviation established and no exculpatory clause applying, POL-RD-02 makes the refund arithmetic rather than discretionary on this METERED fare. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 21.0 + 0.28 x 26.0) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = 27.63, the surge multiplier being read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (1.0) and there being no on-optimal-route ERP, no surcharge and no waiting fee. Refund = charged_total 35.64 - 27.63 = 8.01, rounded UP to SGD 8.05. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and far below 90% of charged_total, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND.

No closure excuses any of this detour. The traffic advisory artifact for this trip, EV-ADVIS-00101-01, is MISSING with weight 0.0: no LTA advisory was issued for the AYE/MCE/ECP corridor in the 10:14-10:59 window. With no advisory there is no road named, no validity window and no shortest_lawful_alternative_km, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and none of the 6.18 km excess is exonerated. The absence is itself the citable fact.

The detour was not rider-requested. All three chat messages carry waypoint_hint = null and the rider names no road, so POL-RD-04's 200 m corroboration test is undecidable on the record and the clause is unavailable. In any event the messages show a rider questioning the route ('hello why we going towards city centre? MBS is the other side') and a driver admitting fault ('sorry boss missed the exit, coming back now') — there is no instruction anywhere in the log that could exonerate the excess.

Nothing resets the 21.0 km baseline. vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply and there is no co-rider distance to exclude; and pickup_amended_at, dropoff_amended_at and amended_optimal_distance_km are all null, so there is no POL-RD-05 relocation recomputation to run. The measured excess of 6.18 km stands unreduced.

The trace is clean and unimpaired for policy purposes: 229 fixes at a 10 s sample interval, 100% coverage, max_gap_sec of 0.0 and an empty gaps array, so POL-RD-07(a)-(c) do not fire and no independent corroboration is required to establish the deviation. Even if it were, the driver's own chat admission supplies it.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. trip_id TRP-00101 and the pickup timestamp match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, and limb (b) is met because the excess clears the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The burden therefore shifts to the driver, who has pointed to no specific exculpatory artifact and no clause to displace the finding.

POL-RD-09 adds nothing to the refund and must not be double-counted against it. The fare_breakdown lists no erp_gantries and carries optimal_route_erp of 0.0, and the trip does not originate at an airport, so there is no off-route ERP, toll or surcharge pass-through correction to stack on top of the POL-RD-02 figure. The rider's recovery is the distance-and-time recomputation alone.

The rider is the filing party, so under the party-relative rule of POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION would leave the $35.64 charge standing against her. The rider-favouring outcome is the partial refund, which strips out the $8.05 that the driver's admitted wrong turn added to a trip that should have cost 27.63.

claims.text: The route deviation is established but falls well short of MATERIAL. On the governing trace the trip ran 27.18 km against a booked optimal of 21.0 km, an excess of 6.18 km (29.4%). That passes POL-RD-01's two establishment tests (greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20%) but is below BOTH materiality gates (greater than 8.0 km and greater than 50%). The deviation is therefore non-material, so the driver_profile check in POL-RD-06 is not even engaged, no FULL_REFUND uplift is available and the remedy is capped at the POL-RD-02 arithmetic partial.

The distance must be measured on the trace. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 27.18 km (EV-GPS-00101) govern over trip_record.actual_distance_km = 27.2 km (EV-TRIP-00101), which is a rounded convenience copy that may not be cited for the threshold test. On the governing field the excess is 6.18 km, exactly as the derived block computes, so the establishment finding stands on a clean, unimpaired 100%-coverage trace with no gaps and a 10 s sample interval - this is not a POL-RD-07 impaired-trace case and no independent corroboration is required.

No repeat-deviation pattern can be established against this driver. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 812 completed_trips_90d (EV-DPROF-00101), which fails POL-RD-06's tests (3 or more flags, or a ratio of 0.05 or more). Combined with the non-material excess, POL-RD-06 is not triggered on any limb: there is no FULL_REFUND uplift, no evidence re-weighing, and no driver-conduct referral.

Whatever refund issues is arithmetic under POL-RD-02 and cannot exceed SGD 8.05. The fare is METERED (EV-FARE-00101.fare_model), so POL-RD-02 governs and POL-RD-11 does not. On the booked optimal of 21.0 km / 26.0 min at surge 1.0: (3.80 + 0.75 x 21.0 + 0.28 x 26.0) = 26.83, plus the 0.80 platform fee = 27.63 recomputed_fare. Refund = 35.64 charged_total - 27.63 = 8.01, rounded UP to SGD 8.05. That is 22.6% of charged_total, so it is a PARTIAL_REFUND, not the FULL_REFUND the rider asks for, and it is well below the SGD 10.00 contested amount.

The only direct evidence of fault is the driver's own contemporaneous in-app message (EV-CHAT-00101, 'sorry boss missed the exit, coming back now'), which describes a simple navigational error corrected within the trip, not a deliberate detour. That is consistent with a single non-material excess and gives no foothold for the POL-RD-06(b) full-refund uplift or the POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral.

ruling.explanation:
This ruling goes to both parties. On 12 July 2026 the trip from Jurong East MRT to Marina Bay Sands ran 27.18 km on the platform's own GPS trace (EV-GPS-00101: 229 fixes, 10 s sampling, 100% coverage, no gaps) against a booked optimal of 21.0 km (EV-TRIP-00101). The excess is 6.18 km, or 29.4%. POL-RD-01 measures on the trace figure, not the rounded 27.2 km convenience copy on the trip record, so the excess is 6.18 km. That clears both establishment tests (over 0.8 km and over 20%), so the deviation IS established.

It does not, however, reach the materiality gates (over 8.0 km, or over 50%), so this is a non-material deviation and the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not engaged. In any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 812 completed trips in 90 days, so no repeat-deviation pattern exists, no full-refund uplift, and no driver-conduct referral arises.

No exculpatory clause rescues the excess. POL-RD-03 cannot run: no LTA traffic advisory was issued for this corridor in the trip window (EV-ADVIS-00101-01 is a MISSING artifact at weight 0.0, and its absence is itself the citable fact). POL-RD-04 fails because every chat message carries no waypoint hint and the rider names no road, so the 200 m corroboration test is undecidable and the rider clearly did not request the detour; the driver himself wrote 'sorry boss missed the exit, coming back now' (EV-CHAT-00101). POL-RD-05 does not apply (no amendment timestamps, amended_optimal_distance_km null) and POL-RD-12 does not apply (vehicle_type RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL).

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02. The fare is METERED, so POL-RD-11 does not govern. Applying the rate card to the booked optimal route: 3.80 + (0.75 x 21.0) + (0.28 x 26.0) = 26.83, times the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, plus the 0.80 platform fee, giving a recomputed fare of 27.63. Charged total was 35.64. Refund = 35.64 - 27.63 = 8.01, rounded up to 8.05. That is above the 0.50 de minimis floor and far below 90% of the charge, so the outcome is a PARTIAL refund of SGD 8.05. No ERP, toll or airport surcharge line exists on this fare, so POL-RD-09 adds nothing and is not double-counted; no driver compensation is due because the billed distance (27.2 km) is not short of the trace figure.

Driver, the wrong turn was your admitted navigational error and you bear the SGD 8.05. Rider, you are refunded the SGD 8.05 that the detour added; the rest of the fare for the trip you actually took stands.

ruling.explanation:
The evidence on both sides agrees on the essentials, and so does this ruling. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00101) records 27.18 km for the trip, and POL-RD-01 makes that figure govern over the trip record's rounded 27.2 km. Against the booked optimal of 21.0 km that is an excess of 6.18 km, or 29.4%. That clears both establishment tests (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%), so the deviation is established — but it falls below both materiality gates (more than 8.0 km and more than 50%), so it is not a material deviation. The trace is clean and unimpaired for policy purposes (229 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps), so no corroboration question arises under POL-RD-07, and the driver's in-app admission ('sorry boss missed the exit, coming back now') confirms the wrong turn in any event.

No exculpatory clause rescues the driver. The detour was not rider-requested: every chat message carries waypoint_hint = null and no road is named, so POL-RD-04's 200 m corroboration test cannot be run and the clause is unavailable (as the evidence stands, the rider was questioning the route, not requesting it). The trip is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply, and the pickup and dropoff were never amended, so POL-RD-05 runs nothing. No LTA traffic advisory was issued for the corridor, so no closure exoneration is available either — though neither party claimed one.

The fare is METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 × 21.0 + 0.28 × 26.0) × surge 1.0, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee = 27.63. Refund = charged_total 35.64 − 27.63 = 8.01, rounded up to SGD 8.05. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and far below 90% of the charge, so the outcome is a partial refund, not the full refund requested. No ERP, toll or airport-surcharge correction is added on top: the fare breakdown lists no gantries and the trip did not originate at an airport, so POL-RD-09 adds nothing.

Two further points. First, no repeat-deviation pattern is established — driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 812 completed trips in 90 days — so there is no POL-RD-06 full-refund uplift and no driver-conduct referral. Second, the driver is owed no compensation: the distance billed (27.2 km) is not less than the trace distance, so POL-RD-04's unbilled-distance limb does not apply. The charge of $35.64 is reduced by $8.05 and the balance stands.

To both parties: the facts here are largely agreed, and the evidence bears them out.

1) The deviation is established. The governing GPS trace (EV-GPS-00101, weight 1.0: 229 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, max gap 0.0, empty gaps array) records 27.18 km driven against a booked optimal of 21.0 km — an excess of 6.18 km, 29.4%. That clears both POL-RD-01 tests (over 20% of optimal and over 0.8 km absolute). The trip record's 27.2 km is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and is not the figure the test runs on. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a)–(c), so no independent corroboration is required and no escalation is triggered on that ground.

2) The deviation is not MATERIAL — it is below both the 50% and 8.0 km gates — so POL-RD-06 is not engaged. The driver's profile shows 0 deviation flags in the trailing 90 days against 812 completed trips, failing both of POL-RD-06's tests. There is therefore no repeat-pattern finding, no FULL_REFUND uplift, and no driver-conduct referral.

3) No exculpatory clause applies. No traffic advisory is on the record — the advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-00101-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and this ruling rests on nothing from it. No rider-requested detour: every chat message carries waypoint_hint null and none names a road, so POL-RD-04's corroboration test cannot be run, and in any event the log shows the rider questioning the route and the driver admitting fault. No pickup/dropoff amendment (pickup_amended_at, dropoff_amended_at and amended_optimal_distance_km are all null), so POL-RD-05 adds nothing. vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply and the 21.0 km baseline stands unreduced.

4) The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02. The fare is METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs and POL-RD-11 does not. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 21.0 + 0.28 x 26.0) x 1.0 surge (read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee = 27.63. Charged_total = 35.64. Refund = 35.64 - 27.63 = 8.01, rounded UP to SGD 8.05. There are no ERP gantries, tolls, surcharges or waiting fees, so POL-RD-09 adds nothing and nothing is double-counted; the rider was also billed for no more distance than the trace records, so there is no unbilled-distance ground for driver compensation. The refund is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and well below 90% of charged_total, so it is a partial refund, not a full one.

The driver's in-app admission ('sorry boss missed the exit, coming back now') and the counterparty statement confirm the wrong turn; they are consistent with this arithmetic and do not change it.

Outcome: PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 8.05 to the rider; the balance of the SGD 35.64 charge stands. Confidence rests on the GPS trace, trip record and fare breakdown, all at weight 1.0.
